core_obligations: Set up the candidate images: put A^vee = qA + q^{-1}A^{-1} and likewise for B and C (proof lines 940-947).

Produce the three identities: combining the cited evaluation and multiplication-table lemmas yields (q+q^{-1})A^vee + (q B^vee C^vee - q^{-1} C^vee B^vee)/(q-q^{-1}) = nu I, and its cyclic analogues (proof lines 948-964).

Conclude existence: since nu I is central, those identities say exactly that A^vee, B^vee, C^vee satisfy the defining relations of the universal algebra, so the homomorphism pi exists; uniqueness follows because A, B, C generate the source (proof lines 965-974).
Compute the images of alpha, beta, gamma: the displayed values nu I follow from the defining relations of those elements together with the three identities (proof lines 974-978).
proof_roadmap: Write down the candidate images and derive the three identities that they satisfy (proof lines 940-964).
Read those identities as the defining relations, get the homomorphism and its uniqueness, and evaluate alpha, beta, gamma (proof lines 965-978).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the universal Askey-Wilson algebra admits a unique F-algebra homomorphism onto the Askey-Wilson algebra Lambda taking A, B, C to the explicit combinations qA + q^{-1}A^{-1} and so on, and that this homomorphism sends alpha, beta and gamma to nu I with nu = (q^2+q^{-2})mu + mu^2 (statement lines 915-937). The proof substitutes the candidate images into the defining relations: two cited lemmas produce the three identities that A^vee, B^vee and C^vee satisfy, and because nu I is central these identities are recognised as the relations of the universal algebra (proof lines 940-971). The step that carries the content is that recognition, since the identities are obtained from a multiplication table rather than assumed; uniqueness and the images of alpha, beta, gamma are then immediate from generation and the defining relations. H2.
